scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to let my 7-year-old brother stay up late instead of making him go to bed. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts the next day. He's really into my friends and thinks they're the coolest, always wanting to hang out with us. My friends don't have little siblings, so they find him super cute and hype him up a lot. Last night, my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until 1 AM. She said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on timeâĢĶhe can put himself to bed. Then my friend came over, and we were goofing around, watching a movie, and being kind of loud. My brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no, go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up, and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now, I would basically have to drag him upstairs. He would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing and exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us. By the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning, he didn't want to get up (even on weekends, he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8 AM) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7, he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later, he won't feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to not force him to go to bed? And why? First, I need to consider the consequences of letting him stay up late. He was cranky the next day, which aligns with what I know about sleep deprivation. But I also think that two hours isn't a huge deal. However, my mom was mad at me for letting him stay up late. On the other hand, I didn't want to have to drag him upstairs and deal with a tantrum, which would have been stressful for everyone. Plus, my friend was over, and I didn't want to ruin the evening. I also need to think about teaching him responsibility. If he knows that staying up late will make him feel bad the next day, maybe he should learn that lesson. But at the same time, he's only 7, and it's my responsibility to make sure he gets enough sleep. Another angle is the impact on our relationship. If I force him to go to bed, he might be upset with me, but if I let him stay up, he's happy in the moment but cranky the next day. It's a bit of a catch-22. I also wonder about the long-term effects. If I consistently let him stay up late, does that set a bad precedent? Or is it just an occasional slip-up? Additionally, I need to consider my mom's perspective. She trusts me to take care of him, and when she found out I let him stay up late, she was upset. That affects our relationship too. So, putting it all together, is it right or wrong to let him stay up late? It seems like there are valid arguments on both sides. On one hand, ensuring he gets enough sleep is important for his well-being and behavior the next day. On the other hand, dealing with a tantrum and the stress of enforcing bedtime might not be worth it in the moment. I also need to think about what's more important: his immediate happiness or his overall well-being. It's a tough call, but I think ensuring he gets enough sleep is more important in the long run, even if it means dealing with some short-term upset. In conclusion, while letting him stay up late might have been easier in the moment, it's probably not the best decision considering the consequences on his mood and behavior the next day. It's important to set boundaries and teach him about responsibility, even if it's hard in the moment.
